title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Michael Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure (IaC/networking), model-serving, observability, and performance objectives. It includes actionable standards, required ownership, and two canonical ADRs that govern competing approaches.

Scope:
Applies to all new and actively maintained services within the Redwood codebase and private deployments (hosted, Dedicated, Private). Exceptions require an ADR and approval from the Platform Architecture Guild.

Principles (top-level):
- Developer ergonomics: API and infra choices should reduce cognitive load for engineers integrating the platform.
- Production-first: Defaults must be safe for production (SLOs, circuit breakers, quotas).
- Observable by default: All services must emit standard metrics, structured logs, and traces.
- Predictable economics: Architectural decisions should consider unit cost (tokens, GPU-hours, egress).
- Backwards compatibility: Major versioning required for breaking API changes; migration guides required.

1) API Standards
- API style: REST+JSON for public-facing endpoints; gRPC recommended for high-throughput internal RPCs between runtime components.
- Versioning: Use semantic versioning in the path for public APIs: /v1/, /v2/. Internal gRPC services must use package-level versioning in proto (e.g., inference.v1).
- Idempotency: POST endpoints performing non-idempotent actions must accept an Idempotency-Key header and persist key for 24h.
- Errors: Use a structured error envelope: {"code": string, "message": string, "details": object}. Maintain an internal canonical list of error codes (400/401/403/404/429/500/503).
- Pagination: Cursor-based pagination for list endpoints with page_size, next_cursor. Avoid offset for large datasets.
- Rate limiting: 429 for quota exceeded; include Retry-After header. Rate limits are implemented at edge and enforced in the API gateway.
- Telemetry: All API handlers must emit metrics: request_count, request_latency_ms (histogram), request_errors by code, request_payload_bytes.
- Contract testing: Public APIs require an OpenAPI spec checked into the repo and automated contract tests in CI.
- Example (response envelope):
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Content-Type: application/json
  {"request_id":"req_123", "data": {...}, "meta": {"model":"redwood-13b-v1", "latency_ms": 120}}

2) Coding standards
- Languages: Primary services use Go (control plane, infra), Rust (runtime hot paths), Python (evals, tooling).
- Linters/formatters: gofmt/golangci-lint, rustfmt/clippy, black/ruff for Python. CI gate requires zero new linter failures.
- Testing: Unit test coverage target 80% for core libraries, 60% for services. All services must include integration tests exercising API contracts and an end-to-end smoke test for deployments.
- Dependency hygiene: Dependabot or Renovate configured; major dependency upgrades require an ADR if they touch runtime or inference libs.
- Code reviews: Minimum one reviewer + approval from the owning team. Changes touching infra IaC or deployment manifests require platform-approver signoff.
- Security coding: Sanitize inputs for parsers; fuzz tests encouraged for model input pipelines. Secrets must never be checked into git.

3) Infrastructure standards (IaC & networking)
- IaC: Terraform is the canonical tool for cloud provisioning. Modules for compute, networking, storage, and monitoring must be published in the internal module registry.
- State management: Terraform state stored in S3 with DynamoDB state locking (AWS) or equivalent. Access to state is restricted to infra and platform CI roles.
- Tagging: All resources must include tags: OwnerTeam, CostCenter, Environment, Project, Service.
- Secrets: Use customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; platform-managed KMS for hosted environments. Secrets referenced via secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager / HashiVault) not in plain text.
- Networking: Default VPC peering patterns for Private customers documented in onprem reference architecture. Minimum network ACLs per service: deny-all except required ports.
- CI/CD: Deployments are automated via the platform pipeline; manual approval required for production infrastructure changes.
- Resource sizing: Standard VM/GPU SKU catalog and a sizing guidance table are maintained in eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity.

4) Model-serving standards
- Packaging: Models must be packaged with a manifest (model-name, version, architecture, tokenizer, quantization profile, input/output schema). Manifest is YAML and stored alongside the model.
- Versioning & compatibility: Every model release increments a semantic model-version. Runtime compatibility matrix (model format -> runtime) must be published.
- Quantization profiles: Approved quantization profiles live in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Use the conservative profile for production unless explicit perf/quality trade-off testing is recorded.
- Cache & batching: Services must expose configuration for KV-cache TTL and batch windows. Defaults: max_batch_size=64, batch_timeout_ms=8 for latency-sensitive routes; these can be tuned per-route with telemetry.
- Fallthroughs & graceful degradation: Define fallback model family per route. If primary model capacity is exhausted or latency SLO violated, route to smaller family (e.g., 13B -> 7B) with a flag in the response explaining degradation.
- Canary & rollouts: Use traffic-splitting policies in the deployment manifest. Canary cadence: 5% for 10 minutes, 25% for 30 minutes, 100% if no quality regressions or errors. Automate rollback on spike in errors or objective regressions.

5) Observability standards
- Metrics: Emit Prometheus-style metrics prefixed with service_*, e.g., service_requests_total, service_request_latency_seconds_bucket, service_model_token_count.
- SLI/SLO: Standard SLIs: availability (request success rate), latency (P50/P95/P99), correctness (quality regression score on canary prompt set). Default SLOs: availability 99.95% monthly, P99 latency <= 500ms for API planning routes (subject to model family).
- Tracing: All RPC boundaries instrumented with OpenTelemetry traces. Include request_id and model_version as trace attributes.
- Logs: Structured JSON logs with keys: ts, level, service, request_id, user_id (if present), msg, extra. Sensitive fields must be redacted before ingestion.
- Dashboards & alerts: Per-service dashboard with errors, latency, token usage, model-fallback rate. Alert thresholds: error rate > 3x baseline for 5m, P99 latency > 2x SLO for 10m, model-fallback rate > 1% for 15m.

6) Performance standards
- Latency objectives: Define per-route latency targets. Example defaults: control-plane APIs P95 < 100ms, inference generation routes P95 < 200ms, P99 targets as noted in Observability.
- Throughput: Document expected throughput per SKU and model family (tokens/sec and concurrent requests). Maintain benchmarking matrix in eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
- Cost/perf tradeoffs: Use Redwood Optimize recommendations for batch sizing and quantization. Performance evaluations must include token-cost curves.
- GPU utilization: Target steady-state utilization 65-85% for dedicated pools; autoscaling triggers at 90% 5-minute average.

7) Ownership & governance
- Owners: Each service must declare a Service Owner (on-call) and an Architecture Owner (longer-term design). Owners are listed in service READMEs and the ownership registry.
- Architecture Guild: Platform Architecture Guild reviews ADRs and cross-cutting changes monthly.
- Exceptions: Any deviation from these standards requires a short ADR with a proposed mitigation and an approval record.

8) Decision records (ADRs)
ADR-2026-01: Model fallback strategy (DECIDED)
- Date: 2026-01-18
- Context: We must maintain availability when large model families are exhausted or latency spikes.
- Decision: Use policy-based fallback routing to progressively degrade to smaller model families. Fallback policy is stored in the routing config and evaluated by the smart router.
- Alternatives considered: 1) Queue requests until capacity available (rejected due to latency/UX). 2) Serve cached prefixes only (insufficient for fresh queries).
- Consequences: Slight decline in output quality during fallback; must include explicit response meta and increase observability on fallback events.

ADR-2025-11: API versioning model (DECIDED)
- Date: 2025-11-03
- Context: Need to support breaking changes while minimizing client disruption.
- Decision: Path-based semantic versioning (e.g., /v1/), with deprecation windows of at least 90 days and automated migration guides.
- Alternatives considered: Header-based versioning (rejected for complexity in caching/CDNs).

9) Example runbook excerpt: Canary rollout for model update
- Preconditions: New model package uploaded to artifact store; canary prompt set and regression suite exist.
- Steps:
  1) Create canary deployment with model-version: X and traffic split 5%.
  2) Run automated canary evals (1000 prompts) and compare quality metrics vs baseline.
  3) Monitor stage dashboard for errors, latency, and model-fallback for 30 minutes.
  4) If quality regressions > threshold or errors spike, rollback to previous model-version and file incident.
  5) Progress traffic per cadence (5% -> 25% -> 100%) if no regressions.
- Ownership: Deploying team + Platform on-call.

10) Templates & artifacts
- Required artifacts for any infra or API change: PR with OpenAPI/proto spec, deployment manifest, canary prompt set (for model changes), cost impact analysis, and roll-forward/rollback playbook.

Appendix: Common CLI snippets
- Terraform plan (example):
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tf-state"
  terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars

- Small sample model manifest (YAML):
  name: redwood-13b-v1
  version: "1.2.0"
  architecture: decoder-only
  tokenizer: redwood-tokenizer-v1
  quantization_profile: conservative-q4
  inputs: |
    - type: text
      max_tokens: 2048

Questions & feedback:
Send questions or proposed changes to the Architecture Guild channel (#architecture-guild) and open an ADR PR in the architecture-and-standards repo.
